items.statement: Let $T$ be an oriented torus and let $([\mu],[\lambda])$ be an ordered basis of $H_1(T;\mathbb Z)$. An unoriented essential simple closed curve on $T$ has homology class $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$ for a unique pair $(p,q)$ up to simultaneous sign, and that pair is primitive: $\gcd(p,q)=1$. Conversely, every primitive pair $(p,q)$ determines an essential simple closed curve, unique up to isotopy and simultaneous reversal of orientation.

items.title: A meridian-preserving torus homeomorphism extends over a solid torus

references.title: Kimihiko Motegi, Dehn surgery on knots: survey, pp. 19–21
Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes, §4.1.1

items.statement: Let $V=D^2\times S^1$ and $V'=D^2\times S^1$ be solid tori, with meridian curves $\mu=\partial D^2\times\{1\}$ and $\mu'=\partial D^2\times\{1\}$. Suppose $h:\partial V\to\partial V'$ is a homeomorphism and there is an isotopy $H_t:\partial V'\to\partial V'$ through homeomorphisms, with $H_0=\mathrm{id}$, such that $H_1(h(\mu))=\mu'$. Then $h$ extends to a homeomorphism $\overline h:V\to V'$. The extension may be chosen to carry the product core $\{0\}\times S^1$ onto the product core of $V'$, and has the same orientation sign as $h$ with respect to the boundary orientations.

items.title: Commuting affine peripheral holonomies factor their logarithms on singular parameter spaces

references.title: Carlo Petronio and Joan Porti, Negatively Oriented Ideal Triangulations and a Proof of Thurston's Hyperbolic Dehn Filling Theorem
references.locator: Lemma 2.6 and its commutativity identity, printed pp. 13–14; Theorem 2.2(1,3); Proposition 3.6

items.statement:
Let $Z$ be a reduced complex analytic space with point $o$, and suppose $u_i,v_i,a_i,b_i$ are holomorphic germs on $Z$ for $1\le i\le k$, with $k<\infty$, $u_i(o)=v_i(o)=0$, $a_i(o)\ne0$ and $\tau_i^0=b_i(o)/a_i(o)\notin\mathbb R$. Suppose the affine maps
$$L_i(w)=e^{u_i}w+a_i,\qquad P_i(w)=e^{v_i}w+b_i$$
commute at every parameter point. Then, after shrinking around $o$, there are holomorphic germs $\tau_i$ such that $v_i=\tau_i u_i$, $\tau_i(o)=\tau_i^0$ and $\operatorname{Im}\tau_i\ne0$ throughout. In particular $u_i=0$ if and only if $v_i=0$, and $v_i/u_i\to\tau_i^0$ as the parameter tends to $o$ through $u_i\ne0$. No smoothness, dimension or rank hypothesis on $Z$ is required.

For $u_i\ne0$, there is a unique real pair $(p_i,q_i)$ solving $p_iu_i+q_iv_i=2\pi i$. With
$$\widetilde u_i=\frac{2\pi i}{p_i+\tau_i^0q_i},$$
one has
$$|\widetilde u_i-u_i|\le\frac{|\tau_i-\tau_i^0|}{|\operatorname{Im}\tau_i^0|}|u_i|.$$
Set $\widetilde u_i=0$ when $u_i=0$. The functions $\widetilde u_i$ are continuous at such points, and $\|\widetilde u-u\|=o(\|u\|)$ as the parameter tends to $o$ through $u\ne0$.

items.title: Closed square-integrable adjoint one-forms on a cusped hyperbolic three-manifold are exact

references.title: Pere Menal-Ferrer and Joan Porti, Twisted cohomology for hyperbolic three manifolds
references.locator: Section 2, particularly Corollary 2.12 and Lemma 2.14; the required complete-manifold analytic implication is also proved locally below

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M=\Gamma\backslash\mathbb H^3$ be an oriented hyperbolic three-manifold with compact complement to finitely many standard torus cusp ends, each isometric to $(T^2\times[0,\infty),dt^2+e^{-2t}g_T)$ for a flat metric $g_T$. The compact case is allowed. Let $E=\mathbb H^3\times_\Gamma\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$ be the adjoint flat bundle. Give its fiber at a basepoint the Hilbert–Schmidt Hermitian product and transport this product by the homogeneous $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)/\mathrm{PSU}(2)$ construction. Write $d_E$ for its flat differential and $\delta_E$ for the metric formal adjoint.

There is $c>0$, depending only on the model normalization, such that every compactly supported smooth $E$-valued one-form satisfies
$$\|d_E\alpha\|_2^2+\|\delta_E\alpha\|_2^2\ge c\|\alpha\|_2^2.$$
Every smooth $E$-valued one-form $\alpha$ with $d_E\alpha=0$ and $\|\alpha\|_2<\infty$ has a smooth square-integrable primitive $b$, with $d_Eb=\alpha$ and $\|b\|_2\le c^{-1/2}\|\alpha\|_2$.

items.title: Simultaneous peripheral full-turn equations have unique small solutions

references.title: William P. Thurston, The Geometry and Topology of Three-Manifolds
references.locator: Section 5.8, the local generalized surgery map; its simultaneous existence and continuity step is proved directly here

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $k\ge1$ and let $\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_k$ be holomorphic on a neighborhood of $0\in\mathbb C^k$, with $\operatorname{Im}\tau_i(0)\ne0$. Put $v_i(u)=u_i\tau_i(u)$. At a coordinate with $u_i\ne0$, define real coefficients $(p_i,q_i)$ by
$$p_i u_i+q_i v_i(u)=2\pi i;$$
at $u_i=0$ define its parameter to be $\infty$ in the one-point compactification $S_i=\mathbb R^2\cup\{\infty\}$.

There are neighborhoods $U$ of $0$ and $V$ of $(\infty,\ldots,\infty)$ in $\prod_iS_i$ for which this parameter map is a homeomorphism $U\to V$. One may take $V=\prod_i(\{(p,q):p^2+q^2>R^2\}\cup\{\infty\})$ for a sufficiently large $R$. Every such tuple has a unique small simultaneous solution, with $u_i=0$ exactly at the unfilled coordinates. Uniformly as the tuple tends to the complete point, writing $w_i=2\pi i/(p_i+q_i\tau_i(0))$ for finite coordinates and $w_i=0$ at $\infty$, one has
$$u_i=w_i+O(|w_i|\|w\|_\infty),\qquad \|u\|_\infty\le\tfrac43\|w\|_\infty.$$
This analytic assertion allows real coefficients of either orientation. Primitive integral coefficients are included, but no geometric completion is asserted by the equations alone.
items.axiom_use: Full AC is retained for the geometric consumers; the finite-dimensional contraction argument itself uses the stated constructive Banach theorem.

items.title: Slopes and generalized fillings on torus cusps

references.title: William P. Thurston, The Geometry and Topology of Three-Manifolds

items.statement:
Let $\overline M$ be a compact connected oriented three-manifold whose boundary is a disjoint union of tori $T_1,\ldots,T_k$. Choose an ordered integral basis $([\mu_i],[\lambda_i])$ for each $H_1(T_i;\mathbb Z)$. A **slope** on $T_i$ is an unoriented isotopy class of essential simple closed curves whose homology class is $p_i[\mu_i]+q_i[\lambda_i]$ for a primitive pair $(p_i,q_i)\in\mathbb Z^2$; simultaneous negation gives the same unoriented slope. The primitive-pair correspondence gives exactly one such slope for each primitive pair modulo sign. The **ordinary Dehn filling** along a tuple of slopes indexed by $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,k\}$ attaches an oriented solid torus $D^2\times S^1$ to each $T_i$, $i\in J$, by an orientation-reversing boundary homeomorphism that sends $[\partial D^2\times\{*\}]$ to the chosen slope. The gluing maps are part of the filling data; $i\notin J$ means that the cusp is left unfilled, denoted by the parameter $\infty$.

For a hyperbolic deformation, the **generalized cone-filling parameter space** at each cusp is the one-point compactification $\mathbb R^2\cup\{\infty\}$ of the real coefficient plane, with $\infty$ denoting the complete cusp. A primitive integral pair $(p_i,q_i)$ is an ordinary smooth filling coefficient. If a realized generalized parameter lies on the ray $g_i=r_i(p_i,q_i)$ with $r_i>0$ and $(p_i,q_i)$ primitive integral, its topological core direction is the ordinary slope $(p_i,q_i)$ and its cone angle is $2\pi/r_i$. Only $r_i=1$ is the ordinary smooth filling; $r_i>1$ describes a cone or orbifold completion and does not turn the nonprimitive vector $g_i$ into a slope.

items.title: The figure-eight complement is a punctured-torus bundle

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the chosen smooth knot-exterior data. Let $K_8$ be the standard figure-eight knot, presented as the boundary of the square plumbing of one positive and one negative Hopf band, with one boundary component. A positive Hopf band is an oriented annulus whose positive normal push-off of its core has linking number $+1$ with the core; a negative Hopf band has linking number $-1$. A square plumbing identifies a square in the boundary collars of the annuli with the four boundary edges alternating between the annuli, then smooths corners. Let $F$ be this plumbed surface, and choose the compact exterior by deleting the interior of the binding neighborhood $N(K_8)\cong\partial F\times D^2$ supplied by the open book; on every page this neighborhood meets the page in an annular collar of $\partial F$. Let $a,b$ be the core curves, ordered so that $a$ is the positive-band core and $a\cdot_F b=+1$. The exterior $E_{K_8}$ fibers over $S^1$ with fiber $F$. With the twist convention that the positive twist $R_a$ sends $a\mapsto a$, $b\mapsto a+b$, and the negative twist $L_b$ sends $a\mapsto a+b$, $b\mapsto b$, the monodromy is $R_a\circ L_b$. After capping $\partial F$ by a disk, its action on the ordered homology basis $([a],[b])$ is represented by $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$.

items.title: Augmented holonomy coordinates at a complete finite-volume hyperbolic structure

references.title: Pere Menal-Ferrer and Joan Porti, Twisted cohomology for hyperbolic three manifolds

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M=\Gamma\backslash\mathbb H^3$ be a connected oriented complete finite-volume hyperbolic three-manifold, with a compact smooth core $N$ and $k\ge1$ standard rank-two torus cusp ends. Thus $M$ is the interior of $N$ and each end has metric $dt^2+e^{-2t}g_i$, where $g_i$ is a flat torus metric. Let $\rho_0:\pi_1(N)\to G=\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)$ be its holonomy. Choose a positively oriented basis $(\mu_i,\lambda_i)$ for each oriented horotorus, so its translation lattice can be normalized to $\langle1,\tau_i^0\rangle$ with $\operatorname{Im}\tau_i^0>0$.

The germ of representations modulo conjugacy at $[\rho_0]$ is a smooth complex manifold of dimension $k$. The functions $s_i(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}^2\rho(\mu_i)$ are local holomorphic coordinates near their values $s_i=4$. Trace squared is well defined in $G$, independently of an $SL_2$ lift.

Augment a nearby representation by choosing one common invariant line for each peripheral subgroup, and quotient these data by simultaneous conjugacy. The germ of this augmented space at the complete representation and its unique peripheral fixed lines is a smooth complex $k$-manifold. It has holomorphic coordinates $u=(u_1,\ldots,u_k)$, where $u_i$ is the eigenvalue-ratio logarithm for $\mu_i$ on the selected line, and the forgetful map is
$$s_i=4\cosh^2(u_i/2).$$
The corresponding logarithms $v_i$ for $\lambda_i$ are holomorphic and satisfy
$$v_i(u)=\tau_i(u)u_i,\qquad \tau_i(0)=\tau_i^0,\qquad \operatorname{Im}\tau_i(u)>0$$
on a sufficiently small neighborhood. In particular $u_i=0$ if and only if $v_i=0$, and for $k=1$ one has $v(u)=\tau^0u+O(u^2)$. No positive or nondegenerate ideal triangulation is assumed. The statement concerns the augmented space, not a single-valued eigenvalue logarithm on the ordinary conjugacy quotient.

items.title: Small augmented holonomy deformations have smooth geometric fillings

references.title: Carlo Petronio and Joan Porti, Negatively Oriented Ideal Triangulations and a Proof of Thurston's Hyperbolic Dehn Filling Theorem
references.locator: Section 2.3, Proposition 2.7 and its entire proof, printed pp. 14–16; the compact realization and the collar normalization are supplied directly below

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M=\Gamma\backslash\mathbb H^3$ be a connected oriented complete finite-volume hyperbolic three-manifold with a compact smooth core and $k\ge1$ disjoint standard torus cusp ends. Choose positively oriented peripheral bases $(\mu_i,\lambda_i)$. Let $\rho_u$, for $u$ near $0$ in $\mathbb C^k$, be the augmented holonomy family supplied by the augmented holonomy-coordinate theorem, based at the complete holonomy $\rho_0$. Thus the logarithms satisfy $v_i(u)=\tau_i(u)u_i$ with $\operatorname{Im}\tau_i(u)>0$.

After shrinking this neighborhood, there are smooth hyperbolic metrics $g_u$ on $M$, possibly incomplete, with holonomy $\rho_u$. They depend smoothly on the real and imaginary parts of $u$ on every compact subset, and $g_0$ is the given complete metric. Each end with $u_i=0$ is a complete finite-volume translation cusp. Each end with $u_i\ne0$ has an explicit developing map onto the punctured tube about its peripheral axis, with the angular and axial periods specified by $u_i,v_i$.

Suppose $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,k\}$ and, for every $i\in J$, a primitive integral pair $(p_i,q_i)$ satisfies
$$p_i u_i+q_i v_i(u)=2\pi i,$$
while $u_i=0$ for $i\notin J$. Then $g_u$ extends across all ends in $J$ to a smooth complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the ordinary Dehn filling whose meridians are $p_i\mu_i+q_i\lambda_i$. For arbitrary supplied orientation-reversing boundary homeomorphisms realizing these same slopes, the resulting topological filling is orientation-preservingly and core-preservingly homeomorphic to this realization, by a homeomorphism equal to the identity on the truncated original manifold. Transporting the realization's smooth structure and metric through this homeomorphism gives the asserted smooth hyperbolic metric on that supplied filling. No assertion is made about a separately prescribed smooth structure for an arbitrary topological gluing. The added cores are ordinary smooth geodesics, with no cone or orbifold singularity. Their lengths are
$$\ell_i=\frac{|u_i|^2\operatorname{Im}\tau_i(u)}{2\pi}>0.$$
Along such filling parameters tending to zero, the metrics converge smoothly to $g_0$ on every compact subset of $M$, the core lengths tend to zero, and the filled volumes tend to $\operatorname{Vol}(M,g_0)$. No ideal triangulation is assumed. This theorem realizes given small holonomy solutions; it does not assert their existence for specified slopes.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K_8$ be the standard figure-eight knot with compact exterior obtained by deleting the binding neighborhood from its open-book presentation and peripheral basis $(\mu,\lambda)$, where $\mu$ is the positive meridian and $\lambda$ is the preferred zero-homology longitude. The exterior fibers over $S^1$ with fiber a once-punctured torus and monodromy fixing its boundary pointwise. Filling along the slope $\lambda$ produces a torus bundle over $S^1$. For the fiber and ordered core basis in the figure-eight plumbing convention, the induced action on the capped torus homology is $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$.

items.statement: Let an oriented finite ideal triangulation of the interior of a compact connected orientable three-manifold have $k\ge1$ ideal vertices, each with torus link. Assign a positive ideal-tetrahedron shape to every tetrahedron. Suppose that around every finite edge the product of its incident complex shape parameters is $1$ and the sum of its dihedral angles is $2\pi$. For each ideal vertex $v$, choose a basis $(\alpha_v,\beta_v)$ of the fundamental group of its torus link and suppose the cusp multipliers satisfy $H(\alpha_v)=H(\beta_v)=1$. Then the face gluings define a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the manifold interior, with one rank-two cusp for each ideal vertex.

items.title: Euclidean length of a slope on a horospherical cusp section

references.title: William P. Thurston, The Geometry and Topology of Three-Manifolds

items.statement: Let $M$ be the interior of a compact connected orientable three-manifold with a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric and torus cusps $C_1,\ldots,C_k$. For a chosen cusp $C_i$, choose a horospherical section $T_i$ and identify its Euclidean universal cover with $\mathbb R^2$ so its deck group is a rank-two translation lattice. A slope on $T_i$ is represented by a primitive lattice vector $v$ modulo sign. Its **Euclidean slope length on the chosen section** is $\ell_{T_i}(v)=\lVert v\rVert$ in the induced Euclidean metric. In upper half-space coordinates, if the section is the quotient of the horosphere of height $h>0$ by lattice $\Lambda$, then $\ell_{T_i}(p,q)=|p u+q w|/h$, where $u,w$ are the translation vectors representing the chosen basis. Replacing height $h$ by $h'>0$ multiplies every slope length by $h/h'$; therefore the length depends on the chosen section and is not an intrinsic number until that section is fixed.

items.statement: Let $N$ be the complement of finitely many disjoint open solid tori in a connected oriented three-manifold, and suppose its interior has a hyperbolic metric. Fix one boundary torus $T$ with primitive peripheral basis $(\mu,\lambda)$. Assume that a neighborhood of this end, after developing into $\mathbb H^3$, is isometric to a punctured radius-$\varepsilon$ tube about a geodesic axis, modulo a translation of length $L>0$ along that axis. Assume that $\lambda$ is the axial translation direction and that $\mu$ is the angular direction making one full turn of angle $2\pi$ about the axis; equivalently, its peripheral holonomy is the identity isometry with the full-turn lift. Then the hyperbolic metric extends smoothly over the ordinary Dehn filling along $\mu$, adding the axis quotient as the core geodesic of length $L$. The same conclusion holds simultaneously for any finite set of ends satisfying these conditions.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be the interior of a compact connected orientable three-manifold with $k\ge1$ torus cusps and a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric. Choose a peripheral basis $(\mu_i,\lambda_i)$ on each cusp. On the augmented holonomy space obtained by selecting one common invariant line on each peripheral subgroup, near the complete structure write $u_i$ and $v_i$ for the logarithms of the eigenvalue ratios of the peripheral holonomies of $\mu_i$ and $\lambda_i$, with branches chosen so $u_i=v_i=0$ at the complete structure. There is a neighborhood of the complete point in the $k$ generalized parameter spheres such that primitive integral filling data $(p_i,q_i)$ in that neighborhood satisfying $p_i u_i+q_i v_i=2\pi i$ at every filled cusp produce a complete finite-volume hyperbolic structure on the ordinary filled manifold. The peripheral full-turn equations are solved simultaneously across the $k$ cusps; unfilled cusps retain their complete parabolic holonomy. No universal numeric length threshold is asserted.

items.title: One-cusped deformation and peripheral logarithm coordinates

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be the interior of a compact connected orientable three-manifold with one torus cusp and a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric. In a neighborhood of its complete holonomy, the representation deformation space modulo conjugacy is a complex one-dimensional manifold, with local coordinate $s=\operatorname{tr}^2\rho(\mu)$ near $s=4$ for a chosen peripheral basis $(\mu,\lambda)$.

Augment a representation by choosing a common invariant line of its peripheral holonomy. The augmented deformation space is a smooth complex curve, with holomorphic eigenvalue-ratio logarithm coordinate $u$ vanishing at the complete point. The forgetful map to the ordinary conjugacy quotient is $s=4\cosh^2(u/2)$. The corresponding logarithm $v(u)$ for $\lambda$ satisfies $v(0)=0$ and $v(u)=\tau u+O(u^2)$. Here $\operatorname{Im}\tau\ne0$; it is positive for a positively oriented basis of the oriented horotorus, and changes sign if the basis orientation is reversed. In particular the eigenvalue logarithm is a coordinate on the augmented space, rather than a single-valued holomorphic coordinate on the ordinary quotient.

The pair $(u,v)$ records the local generalized filling parameters. The primitive slope equation $p u+q v(u)=2\pi i$ has its full-turn holonomy meaning for ordinary smooth filling when $\gcd(p,q)=1$; sufficiently large primitive coefficients admit such small solutions and smooth complete hyperbolic fillings. Nonprimitive ray parameters are not ordinary slopes.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be the interior of a compact connected orientable three-manifold with $k\ge1$ torus cusps and a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric. Choose an ordered peripheral basis on each cusp. For cusp $i$, let the generalized filling parameter sphere be $S_i=\mathbb R^2\cup\{\infty\}$, with $\infty$ denoting the complete cusp and primitive integral pairs modulo sign denoting ordinary slopes. There is a neighborhood $U$ of $(\infty,\ldots,\infty)$ in $\prod_{i=1}^k S_i$ such that every tuple in $U$ whose finite coordinates are primitive integral slopes determines a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the corresponding ordinary Dehn filling; coordinates equal to $\infty$ remain unfilled complete cusps. Consequently, one may choose neighborhoods $U_i$ of $\infty$ with $\prod_i U_i\subseteq U$, and only finitely many primitive integral pairs at each cusp lie outside $U_i$. Thus every simultaneous filling whose slopes all lie in their respective $U_i$ is hyperbolic. Nonprimitive ray parameters may describe cone or orbifold completions but are not ordinary smooth fillings. No universal numeric length threshold or universal bound on the number of exceptional slopes is asserted.

items.statement: Let $K_8$ be the standard figure-eight knot, let $E_{K_8}$ be the exterior obtained by deleting the binding neighborhood from its open-book presentation, and use the positive meridian $\mu$ and preferred longitude $\lambda$. The exterior admits a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric obtained by gluing two regular ideal tetrahedra, of total volume $2v_3=6\Lambda(\pi/3)\approx2.02988$, where $v_3=3\Lambda(\pi/3)$ is the volume of one regular ideal tetrahedron and $\Lambda$ is the Lobachevsky function. The ordinary zero filling along $\lambda$ is a torus bundle over $S^1$ with monodromy matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ on the capped fiber homology, and the filled manifold admits no complete hyperbolic metric.
